title: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce - Business Studies - Production
exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The process of creating goods and providing services to satisfy human wants is known as
questions.explain: In business studies, **production** is fundamentally defined as any economic activity that creates value by creating goods and providing services that satisfy human wants.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In the chain of distribution, the process of production is completely achieved only when the goods
options: are priced at the highest value
are safely kept in a warehouse
have successfully reached the final consumer
have been thoroughly inspected by the manager
questions.explain: Production is not considered complete merely at the factory level. It is fully completed only when the goods or services **reach the final consumer** to satisfy their needs.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Production is broadly divided into three major categories to cover all economic activities. These categories are
questions.explain: All production activities are broadly classified into **Industry** (creation/extraction), **Commerce** (distribution/exchange), and **Services** (direct and indirect assistance).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Industries involved in obtaining raw materials from the earth, rivers, or seas in their natural state are classified as
questions.explain: **Extractive industries** deal with pulling raw materials directly from nature, forming the primary stage of production.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following occupational activities belongs strictly to the extractive industry?
questions.explain: **Crude oil drilling** extracts natural resources directly from the earth, making it a classic example of an extractive industry. The other options involve construction or manufacturing.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The type of industry responsible for converting primary raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods is called
questions.explain: A **manufacturing industry** takes the raw materials (like raw cocoa or cotton) obtained by the extractive industry and processes them into finished consumer goods (like chocolate or clothes).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A business that buys logs of timber from a forest reserve and processes them into wooden furniture is operating in the
questions.explain: By processing and changing the form of the raw timber into a usable finished product (furniture), the business acts as a **manufacturing industry**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Industries that assemble already manufactured components into major physical structures such as bridges, roads, and houses belong to the
questions.explain: **Constructive industries** focus on assembling and building heavy infrastructure and housing using materials produced by the manufacturing industry.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All of the following activities are examples of the constructive industry EXCEPT
questions.explain: Railway tracks, stadiums, and dams are heavy infrastructure projects (constructive). **Baking loaves of bread** is the creation of a consumable product from raw ingredients, which falls under manufacturing.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Intangible activities performed by individuals or organizations to satisfy human needs, such as healthcare, education, and banking, are categorized under
questions.explain: Unlike goods, which are physical objects, **services** are intangible economic activities that people perform to satisfy the needs of others.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: How does Commerce act as a vital component of the production process?
options: It legally prevents goods from crossing international borders.
It distributes the manufactured goods, bridging the gap to consumers.
It is responsible for planting the agricultural seeds in the farm.
It destroys obsolete products in the warehouse.
questions.explain: Because production is only complete when goods reach the consumer, **Commerce** is an essential part of production because it facilitates the physical distribution and trade of the goods produced.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A negative effect of large-scale industrial production on the environment is
options: the pollution of air and water bodies
an increase in a country's foreign reserves
the improvement of the standard of living
questions.explain: While production brings economic benefits, one major negative effect on the environment is **pollution** (such as toxic emissions in the air and waste dumped into water bodies).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following represents a positive socio-economic effect of industrial production in a society?
options: Severe deforestation and loss of wildlife
Provision of massive employment and wealth creation
Overcrowding and congestion in industrial cities
questions.explain: Industrial production positively impacts society through the **provision of employment** for the population and the **creation of wealth** leading to a better standard of living.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In the classification of production, agricultural farming belongs to the __________ industry, while tailoring belongs to the __________ industry.
questions.explain: Farming extracts resources directly from the soil (**extractive**), whereas tailoring transforms raw fabric into finished clothes (**manufacturing**).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When factories do not properly manage their industrial by-products, society directly suffers from
options: an instant reduction in income tax rates
severe health hazards and environmental degradation
questions.explain: Improper waste disposal by industries has a damaging effect, leading to **severe health hazards and environmental degradation** for the local community.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which list correctly represents the three main sub-divisions of Industry within the concept of production?
questions.explain: Under the syllabus categorization, Industry is composed of three specific branches: **Extractive, Manufacturing, and Constructive** industries.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Essential auxiliary services like warehousing, advertising, transport, and insurance are formally classified as part of production under
questions.explain: Activities such as warehousing, advertising, and transport are **Aids to trade**, making them a vital part of **Commerce**, which forms one of the three broad pillars of production.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is considered an indirect service in production?
options: A barber cutting a client's hair
A doctor prescribing medication to a patient
A police officer maintaining general law and order in the city
A tutor teaching a student at home
questions.explain: Direct services are paid for directly by the individual receiving them (like a barber or doctor). **A police officer** provides an indirect service because they protect the society at large and are paid collectively via government taxes.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies
